Brief Description

About Us

At FreshDirect
, we are reinventing the grocery experience.

Since day one, our mission has been simple: bring the best, freshest food directly from the farm to people’s homes — faster, fresher, and smarter than anyone else.

We’re not just a food company. We’re a technology-powered, customer-obsessed team building one of the most innovative end-to-end food supply chains in the industry. From proprietary routing systems to our state-of-the-art fulfillment center, every part of our business is designed to deliver unmatched quality, convenience, and care.

We partner directly with farmers, fishermen, and artisans to source the highest quality ingredients — then use smart data, automation, and logistics to deliver them at peak freshness.

It’s grocery shopping reimagined — and we’re just getting started.

If you’re passionate about innovation, care deeply about what people eat, and want to help build the future of food, we’d love to meet you.

The Role

Lead, mentor, and grow a multidisciplinary team of full stack, React Native, and senior backend engineers across multiple positions and geographies.
Own delivery, quality, and reliability across all four last-mile applications, balancing roadmap commitments with technical health.
Set technical direction, standards, and best practices for code quality, testing, security, and operational excellence.
Conduct hiring, performance management, career development, and capacity planning for the engineering organization.

What You’ll Do

Technical Direction & Architecture

Drive system architecture decisions across Java/J2EE services, microservices, React and React Native front ends, and GCP-based infrastructure.
Guide the design and development of scalable RESTful APIs and backend services.
Oversee data architecture and performance across PostgreSQL, MongoDB, and Firebase, including caching and query optimization.
Champion CI/CD pipelines, automation, observability, and DevOps maturity across teams.
Ensure compliance with modern security standards and best practices (including PCI where applicable).

What You’ll Bring

12+ years of professional software engineering experience, with 4+ years leading and managing engineering teams (including managers and/or senior engineers).
Proven track record delivering and operating large-scale, high-transaction web and mobile applications in production.
Deep expertise in core Java/J2EE and related frameworks (Spring, JPA, JMS).
Strong experience designing and developing RESTful services and microservices architectures.
Solid command of front-end fundamentals (HTML, JavaScript, CSS) and modern JS frameworks, especially React.
Experience overseeing mobile application delivery, ideally React Native across iOS and Android.
Hands-on background with relational and NoSQL data stores (PostgreSQL, MongoDB, Firebase) and performance/query optimization.
Deep understanding of cloud services, with GCP strongly preferred.
Experience with CI/CD tooling, build automation, and caching frameworks.
Practical Linux knowledge and shell scripting.
Strong problem-solving skills and adaptability in fast-changing requirements.
Excellent communication, interpersonal, and cross-team collaboration skills, with experience leading globally distributed teams.
Experience in e-commerce, logistics, or high-transaction-processing environments.
Knowledge of AlloyDB, SQL/PLSQL, and database design.
Familiarity with additional JS frameworks and build tools, and CSS frameworks (Bootstrap, Sass/LESS).
Exposure to routing, geospatial, or timeslot/scheduling systems.
Familiarity with system administration concepts (load balancers such as F5, firewalls, Akamai/CDN).
Knowledge of PCI compliance and broader security standards.
Exposure to data science and machine learning applied to logistics or personalization.

Nice to have:

Experience in e-commerce, logistics, or high-transaction-processing environments.
Knowledge of AlloyDB, SQL/PLSQL, and database design.
Familiarity with additional JS frameworks and build tools, and CSS frameworks (Bootstrap, Sass/LESS).
Exposure to routing, geospatial, or timeslot/scheduling systems.
Familiarity with system administration concepts (load balancers such as F5, firewalls, Akamai/CDN).
Knowledge of PCI compliance and broader security standards.
Exposure to data science and machine learning applied to logistics or personalization.

Our Values at FreshDirect

We live these values every day:

A Passion for our customers

Our customers are at the heart of everything we do. We listen, innovate, and act quickly to exceed expectations with every order and interaction.

One team, one mission

Everyone contributes & every role matters. We break silos, lift each other up, and share a relentless focus on delivering results. That way, we win together.

Delivering excellence, every time

We take pride in the quality of our food, service, and the experience we create. Our team goes above and beyond to earn trust and guarantee 100% freshness.

Act with integrity

We operate with honesty, respect, and accountability in how we treat our customers, teammates, and partners. We own our outcomes and always do what’s right, even when no one is watching.

Make fast, bold decisions

We challenge the status quo, embrace technology, and take smart risks to build a better future. At the same time, we stay true to our NYC roots and care for our community.

We love food. Yes, literally all of us.

What You’ll Love About Working Here

A fast-paced, innovative environment where ideas turn into action
Opportunities for growth — many of our leaders have risen through the ranks
Direct impact on how thousands of customers experience food every day

We embrace an in-office culture, composed of individuals who thrive on the collaboration and energy that comes from working together in a shared space. jobs.title: Director, Engineering, Android Device Platforms
jobs.description:
Join PatientPoint to be part of a dynamic team creating change in and around the doctor’s office. As a leading digital health company, we innovate
to positively impact
patient behaviors. Our purpose-driven approach offers an inspirational career
opportunity where you can contribute to improving health outcomes for millions of patients nationwide.

Location:
Remote within the United States
Travel Required
: Approximately 2–4 weeks per year
Job Summary

As Director of Engineering, Device Products & Operations, you will oversee software engineering across PatientPoint’s device-side product areas — field operations and device management tooling, exam-room patient engagement technology, waiting-room displays, and back-office systems — all running on Android and BrightSign devices in clinical and on-site settings.  
You will be the Engineering Manager for a mix of senior Engineering Leads and individual-contributor engineers, owning hiring, performance, and career growth directly, and stepping into the Engineering Lead’s technical-direction role yourself where a team needs it.  
This is a hands-on role: you’ll stay close to the code, contribute directly where it matters, champion AI-assisted and agentic ways of working across your teams, and make credible architecture calls — across Android (including custom Android ROM), AWS (IoT Core, Lambda, Bedrock AgentCore), and JavaScript/React front-ends — alongside staff engineers and PatientPoint’s Architecture Review Board.  
What  You’ll  Do

Own engineering outcomes across PatientPoint’s device product areas — field operations tooling, exam-room technology, waiting-room displays, and back-office systems.  
Serve as the Engineering Manager for a mix of senior Engineering Leads and individual-contributor engineers — owning hiring, performance, and career growth directly — and step into the Engineering Lead’s technical-direction role yourself where a team needs it.  
Stay close to the code: lead code reviews, contribute directly where needed, and guide teams on technical best practices.  
Champion AI-assisted and agentic engineering practices — in your own work, across your teams’ day-to-day development, and in the AI-powered capabilities we build into our products (e.g., automated device diagnostics).  
Coordinate priorities and dependencies across three or more concurrently active product areas with different tech stacks and team maturity.  
Represent the device product areas in cross-org architecture reviews (ARB/RFCs) and make architecture trade-off calls alongside staff-level engineers.  
Help engineers and Engineering Leads grow in their roles and career paths at PatientPoint.  
Represent engineering as an executive peer to Product and Design leadership in trio-level and product-level planning.  
Manage a blended team of full-time and contract engineers, onshore and offshore.  
Partner with senior engineering leadership on organizational design and resourcing, and represent the device product areas’ health and staffing needs to executive stakeholders.  

What We Need

12+ years of software engineering experience, including 4+ years leading engineering teams, with experience owning outcomes across three or more concurrent product areas or technical domains.  
Experience managing a blended team of senior technical/architectural leads, individual-contributor engineers, and full-time/contract engineers (onshore and offshore) — including direct hiring, performance, and career-growth responsibility.  
Hands-on experience building and operating software for Android — including custom Android ROMs, Mobile Device Management (MDM) and IoT device communication protocols (e.g., AWS IoT Core, BLE/GATT) — deep enough to credibly evaluate architecture and code from staff-level engineers. Working understanding of the constraints these devices run under: limited memory, storage, and processing power; intermittent network connectivity; remote update and rollback without a technician on site; and fleets spanning legacy to current Android releases.  
Experience with front-end frameworks (JavaScript or TypeScript), and with the backend services (e.g., Kotlin/HTTP4k, Node/serverless, or equivalent JVM/Node microservices) that support device fleets.  
Hands-on use of AI-assisted development tools (e.g., GitHub Copilot, Cursor, Claude) in your own workflow, and experience driving adoption of AI-assisted or agentic practices across an engineering team.  

Desired Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in computer science, engineering, information systems, or a related field  
Experience operating in or leading a product-operating-model / product-trio structure.  
Comfort partnering with a central architecture function (ARB, RFC process, or equivalent) on org-wide technical standards.  
Familiarity with Android and BrightSign device-platform tooling — hybrid apps that pair native Android with web/JavaScript content rendered inside the native shell, signage-management platforms (e.g., SignageOS, Broadsign) layered on BrightSign hardware, APK distribution, and OS-upgrade programs.  
Experience with AI SDLC practices and guiding or contributing to AI-powered product capabilities (e.g., automated device diagnostics, self-healing device operations, or similar agentic/AI-driven features).  
Experience in vulnerability management and remediation, including SAST/SCA/DAST triage and architecture-level security reviews, across a device fleet or distributed system.  
Experience in healthcare or another regulated industry, including working knowledge of healthcare compliance requirements (PHI handling, HIPAA awareness) and how they influence architecture decisions for patient-facing devices.  
Experience developing, tracking, and promoting a data-driven delivery framework such as DORA metrics (Deployment Frequency, Lead Time for Changes, Mean Time to Restore, Change Failure Rate).  
Hands-on background in AOSP/customized Android ROM work (init/bootstrap-level work, root shell operations, AIDL/IPC).  
Hands-on experience with agent-orchestration frameworks or patterns (e.g., multi-agent/orchestrator-subagent pipelines, MCP-based tool access, AWS Bedrock AgentCore, Strands Agents, or similar).  
Experience with Kotlin Multiplatform or similar cross-platform native architectures (shared business logic across Android, JVM/Linux, and other targets).  

What  You’ll  Need to Succeed

Ability to direct and lead teams to deliver product features and continuously improve software quality and development practices.  
Comfortable being a technical anchor, not just a manager — able to hold your own on architecture trade-offs with staff-level engineers, and to jump into code when needed.  
Strong ability to develop talent and help engineers grow into bigger roles.  
Excellent collaboration and communication skills, working effectively across Product, Design, and Architecture teams.  
Proven ability to establish engineering best practices, operational excellence, and execution discipline while fostering collaboration and innovation.  
Experience leading through organizational change and team transitions.  

Base Salary Band: $185,600 - $257,400

D-Wave Quantum Inc. (NASDAQ: QBTS)

is a leader in the development and delivery of quantum computing systems, software, and services. It is the world’s first commercial supplier of quantum computers, and the first and only to offer dual-platform quantum computing products and services, spanning both annealing and gate-model quantum computing technologies. D-Wave’s mission is to help customers realize the value of quantum today through enterprise-grade systems available on-premises and via its Leap™ quantum cloud service, which offers 99.9% availability and uptime. More than 100 organizations across commercial, government, and research sectors trust D-Wave to address complex computational challenges using quantum computing. Learn more about realizing the value of quantum computing today and how D-Wave is shaping the quantum-driven industrial and societal advancements of tomorrow: www.dwavequantum.com.

D-Wave is seeking an experienced Vice President of Systems Engineering to build and lead a world-class Systems Engineering organization supporting our Gate Model Quantum Computing program. In this leadership role, you will define the systems engineering strategy, architecture, integration, and technical execution required to deliver scalable, fault-tolerant quantum computing systems.

You will lead the organization responsible for ensuring the Quantum Processing Unit (QPU), control electronics, cryogenic systems, calibration software, runtime software, cloud services, and system monitoring operate as a single, integrated platform that meets product, performance, and reliability objectives.

Build, lead, mentor, and grow a high-performing Systems Engineering organization, including engineering managers and senior technical leaders

Represent Systems Engineering as a senior technical leader with executive leadership, customers, strategic partners, and external stakeholders

Demonstrated success defining system architectures and delivering large-scale products from concept through commercialization

Job Type

Full-time

Description

We are seeking a visionary Director, Data Engineering to architect the "data set of the future." This role is not just about reporting; it is about building the scalable, AI-ready infrastructure that will fuel our next generation of manufacturing innovation. You will move the organization beyond traditional data warehousing to a robust Data Lakehouse architecture, ensuring our enterprise data—from shop floor to point-of-sale—is clean, real-time, and ready for advanced GenAI and predictive modeling.

The ideal candidate is a technologist who fluently bridges the gap between the plant floor and the front office. You will be responsible for integrating complex operational data with high-velocity sales and commercial data to create a unified ecosystem. By connecting factory efficiency directly to customer demand and market trends, you will enable us to pivot from reactive operations to a truly predictive enterprise.

Key Responsibilities

Architecting the Future: Define and execute a data infrastructure roadmap centered on a Lakehouse architecture that integrates structured and unstructured data, enabling both real-time operational analytics and high-scale AI/ML workloads.
AI-Ready Foundation: Establish the data governance, cataloging, and lineage frameworks necessary to power secure, trusted AI models and Large Language Models (LLMs) across the enterprise.
Manufacturing Integration: Partner with OT and Engineering teams to ingest and operationalize IIoT and supply chain data, creating a unified data ecosystem that drives predictive maintenance and factory floor efficiency.

JOB TITLE

Director, Systems Engineering

LOCATION

Worcester

DEPARTMENT NAME

Infrastructure Services and Architecture

DIVISION NAME

Job Description Summary

Reporting to the Assistant Chief Technology Officer, Infrastructure Services and Architecture, the Director of Systems Engineering will oversee the operation, administration, and engineering of the university's systems environment, including servers, storage, cloud computing, and virtualization, along with infrastructure DevOps, application system and security support, and Campus Safety Services. Information technology plays a vital and ever-expanding role in the institutional mission.

The institution's information technology environment is highly distributed and diverse, and the Director of Systems Engineering must be an adept and informed leader who can offer strategic vision, comprehensive planning, and direct technical involvement alongside the engineers who report to the role. This senior leadership role is responsible for ensuring the confidentiality, integrity, and availability of the systems that support the university's educational and operational objectives, and for the reliability of the physical access control, video surveillance, emergency radio, and emergency phone systems that support campus safety.

Job Description

Strategic Leadership and Team Development

Develop and implement a comprehensive systems strategy aligned with the university's goals and objectives.
Provide strategic direction for systems operations and administration, storage, cloud computing and virtualization, application system and security support, and Campus Safety Services.
Collaborate with the Assistant CTO and other senior leaders to prioritize systems initiatives and align them with institutional priorities.
Develop staff, set clear performance expectations, and manage workload and operational tasks across the systems team.
Work with other groups within IT and other business units as needed to develop solutions for unique system requirements, including technical and regulatory requirements.

Systems, Storage, Virtualization, and Cloud Engineering

Working directly with the Systems Engineers who report to this role, direct the design, implementation, and management of the university's physical and virtual server infrastructure, enterprise storage and backup platforms, and AWS and Azure cloud environments.
Participate actively in solution design, technical review, and implementation planning alongside the engineering team.
Ensure efficient utilization of resources through effective virtualization, capacity planning, and lifecycle management.
Lead the evaluation, selection, and adoption of new platform technologies to enhance systems capabilities.
Ensure new implementations are documented, supportable, and aligned with institutional standards and architecture.

Systems Operations and Administration

Oversee the team that performs the day-to-day operation and administration of the university's systems environment, ensuring the stability, availability, and performance of all system components.
Ensure all key services, systems, and components are under appropriate monitoring and alerting.
Ensure operating system patching, firmware maintenance, and lifecycle activities are performed on a defined and predictable cadence.
Ensure that all documentation and databases are up to date and accurate, including asset inventory and configuration records.
Serve as the senior escalation point for the team during major incidents, directing the response, restoring service, and driving root cause analysis and preventive action to completion.
Ensure all systems incidents and service requests are fully resolved within the applicable SLA and maintain open lines of communication with other ITS teams, including the Service Desk.

DevOps, Automation, and Process Improvement

Manage the DevOps resource supporting the infrastructure organization, receiving strategic DevOps and automation requirements from the Assistant CTO and directing the work accordingly.
Identify commonly performed actions, repeated requests, and recurring requirements across every area reporting to this role, including systems operations, storage, virtualization, cloud, application system support, and Campus Safety Services.
Define, document, and standardize the processes behind that work so it can be measured and performed consistently by both full-time employees and the managed service provider.
Identify and prioritize the automation opportunities with the greatest return on team efficiency, and direct their design, build, and adoption.
Measure the effect of automation and process improvement on toil, cycle time, and error rates, and adjust priorities based on results.
Promote the adoption of automation and consistent operating practice across the teams reporting to this role.

Application System and Security Support

Own the systems and middleware layer beneath the university's enterprise and departmental applications, including database platforms, web services, and load balancing.
Ensure that these platforms are appropriately sized, patched, monitored, hardened, and recoverable.
Partner with application owners and the Office of Information Security to remediate vulnerabilities and apply security controls at the system and middleware layer.
Coordinate maintenance windows and upgrade planning with application stakeholders to minimize disruption to academic and administrative operations.

Campus Safety Services

Oversee the technology, operation, and support of campus safety systems, including physical card access, video surveillance, emergency radios, and the emergency phone system.
Ensure the security, reliability, and availability of these physical security and life-safety systems.
Oversee deployment, upgrade, and lifecycle planning for campus safety technology, including coverage associated with building renovation and construction projects.
Collaborate with Campus Police, Facilities, and external vendors and integrators to align technology capability with campus safety requirements.

Security, Compliance, and Resilience

Ensure all systems components meet institutional security and compliance requirements, and implement best practices for securing server, storage, virtualization, cloud, and campus safety infrastructure.
Ensure system designs and procedures are aligned with, and capable of enforcing, university policies and best practices.
Ensure backup, recovery, and business continuity capabilities are designed, documented, and regularly tested against defined recovery objectives.
Ensure vulnerabilities are remediated within institutional service level targets and provide the Information Security operations team with the access and tooling required to identify, locate, and isolate systems involved in security incidents.
Support audit activity and the production of control evidence, and assist Information Security in drafting policies that overlap with the systems team.

Budget, Vendor, and Resource Management

Develop and manage the operating and capital budget for the systems team and Campus Safety Services technology.
Ensure efficient use of resources and identify opportunities for cost savings and license optimization.
Oversee vendor relationships and negotiate contracts for systems, storage, cloud, and campus safety related services and products, interacting directly with vendors, resellers, and integrators.
Plan and forecast refresh and renewal cycles to support multi-year budget development.

Performs all other duties and responsibilities as assigned or directed by the supervisor.

Qualifications

4-year bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Engineering, Information Systems, or Information Technology, or equivalent experience. A bachelor's degree in Information Technology, Computer Science, Engineering, Information Systems, or a related field is preferred.
Minimum of 7 years of experience, including direct leadership of a systems, infrastructure, or operations team.
Strong leadership and team management skills, with the ability to develop and retain technical staff.
Excellent strategic thinking and planning abilities.

new_jobs.description:
About Machina Labs

Engineering moves at software speed. Manufacturing doesn’t. Yet.

Machina Labs is changing that. We build intelligent, software-defined factories that produce complex metal structures directly from digital design. By integrating advanced metal forming, robotics, and automated production inside a flexible factory architecture, we enable customers to move from prototype to production in weeks, not years.

Backed by Lockheed Martin, Toyota, and NVIDIA, we’re building the manufacturing infrastructure that defense, aerospace, and advanced mobility programs will run on.

If you want to work on hard problems that matter and see them fly, drive, and defend, this is the place.

About The Role

Machina Labs is looking for a Director of Infrastructure & Security to build the secure, scalable technology foundation for our next stage of growth.

You’ll lead enterprise IT, cloud and DevOps infrastructure, cybersecurity, compliance, and physical security systems across Machina Labs’ commercial operations and Machina Bellator, our defense-focused subsidiary.

This is a build role. You’ll inherit capable teams and an existing technology foundation, but there is significant work ahead as Machina scales. You will define the infrastructure and security roadmap, strengthen our defense-compliant environment, build our Security Engineering capability, and ensure our systems can scale without slowing down the engineers and operators who rely on them.

You’ll report to the VP of Engineering – Software & IT and partner closely with leaders across Engineering, Manufacturing, Operations, EHS, Legal, and the broader business.

This is a player-coach role for someone who can set strategy and build organizations while staying close enough to the technology to dive in when it matters.

What You’ll Do

Set the infrastructure and security strategy. Define and execute the strategy for IT, cloud infrastructure, cybersecurity, and security systems across Machina Labs and Machina Bellator as our teams, facilities, and defense programs scale.
Lead and grow the organization. Lead the IT and DevOps teams, define the organization needed for the next stage of growth, develop existing leaders, and build the Security Engineering function from the ground up.
Scale cloud and DevOps infrastructure. Guide the architecture, reliability, security, and cost management of our AWS environment in partnership with DevOps and Software Engineering. Establish scalable approaches to infrastructure as code, CI/CD, observability, and production operations.
Build our cybersecurity capability. Establish and mature security operations across endpoint protection, SIEM and logging, threat detection and response, vulnerability management, incident response, and security architecture.
Lead technical defense compliance. Own the technology strategy, controls, documentation, and audit readiness required to support CMMC, NIST SP 800-171, DFARS, ITAR/EAR, and other requirements associated with our defense and aerospace programs.
Own physical security technology. Partner with EHS, which owns the broader physical security program, to architect and operate the technology behind facility security — including access control, surveillance, identity integration, monitoring, and related security systems.
Establish policy and governance. Partner with Legal, EHS, Compliance, Engineering, and Operations to create pragmatic security and IT policies that protect the company and satisfy customer and regulatory requirements without creating unnecessary friction.

What We’re Looking For

10+ years of experience across infrastructure, enterprise IT, cybersecurity, DevOps, or related technical functions, including significant experience leading technical teams and senior leaders.
Experience owning infrastructure and/or security in a complex engineering, manufacturing, aerospace, defense, or similarly regulated environment.
Demonstrated ability to build and scale technology functions, operating models, and teams — not simply operate established systems.
Strong working knowledge of modern enterprise IT, cloud infrastructure, networking, identity and access management, and cybersecurity architecture.
Experience with AWS or comparable cloud environments and modern DevOps practices.
Experience building or operating cybersecurity programs spanning areas such as endpoint security, logging/SIEM, vulnerability management, incident response, and detection and response.
Experience working with security and compliance frameworks such as CMMC or comparable regulated environments.
A builder mindset. You’re comfortable moving between long-term strategy, organizational design, and the technical details required to get something working.

Nice to Have

Experience in defense, aerospace, or another environment handling CUI, export-controlled information, or classified programs.
Experience taking an organization through CMMC certification or a comparable cybersecurity compliance program.
Experience working in ITAR/EAR-controlled environments.
Experience designing technology infrastructure for manufacturing facilities, engineering labs, or other complex physical environments.
Experience with physical security technologies such as access control, video surveillance, visitor management, and integrated identity systems.
Experience scaling infrastructure and security through a period of rapid company and facility growth.

$200,000 - $250,000 a year

The base salary range for this role is dependent on experience, qualifications, and overall alignment with the scope of the position.

In addition to base compensation, Machina Labs offers a competitive benefits package and stock option participation.
